site.name: VuloMail
site.tagline: Every email and text your WordPress site sends, actually delivered.
site.description: VuloMail is a free WordPress plugin that sends your site's email and SMS through the provider you already use, fails over to a backup, logs every message, and texts you when something breaks.

items.label: All features
items.desc: Everything VuloMail does, on one page

items.label: SMS alerts
items.desc: 18 alerts for your site, store and customers

items.label: Security & privacy
items.desc: Encrypted keys, private logs, no tracking

items.desc: Install, connect and send a test in minutes

providers.name: SMTP
providers.blurb: Any SMTP account. Works with Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Amazon SES, Zoho and most others.
providers.note: Uses the PHPMailer bundled with WordPress. Other plugins can still adjust content, but none can redirect the message.

providers.name: SendGrid
providers.blurb: Transactional email over SendGrid's v3 Mail Send API.
providers.note: Success is HTTP 202. The provider's message id is kept for you to look up later.

providers.name: Mailgun
providers.blurb: Mailgun's messages API, in the US or EU region.
providers.note: The sending domain is validated as a hostname before it is ever placed in a URL.

providers.name: Brevo
providers.blurb: Brevo's transactional email API.
providers.note: Any 2xx response from Brevo counts as accepted.

providers.name: Postmark
providers.blurb: Postmark's email API with message streams.
providers.note: Postmark reports some failures as HTTP 200, so VuloMail also checks ErrorCode.

providers.name: Elastic Email
providers.blurb: Elastic Email transactional API.
providers.note: Create one in Elastic Email, under Settings → API.

providers.name: Mailjet
providers.blurb: Mailjet transactional email API.
providers.note: Find both keys in Mailjet, under Account Settings → API Key Management.

providers.name: MailerSend
providers.blurb: MailerSend transactional email API.
providers.note: Needs the "Email: full access" or "Email: send" permission. Create one in MailerSend, under Settings → API Tokens.

providers.name: Maileroo
providers.blurb: Maileroo transactional email API.
providers.note: Open your domain in Maileroo, then its Sending Keys page.

providers.name: Mailtrap
providers.blurb: Mailtrap transactional Email Sending API.
providers.note: Create it under Settings → API Tokens, with admin permission on the sending domain.

providers.name: Mandrill
providers.blurb: Mandrill (Mailchimp Transactional) API.
providers.note: Needs a paid Mailchimp plan with Transactional Email. Create the key under SMTP & API Info.

providers.name: Netcore Email API
providers.blurb: Netcore (formerly Pepipost) transactional email API v5.
providers.note: Find it under Settings → Integrations → API.

providers.name: Resend
providers.blurb: Resend transactional email API.
providers.note: A sending-only key is enough.

providers.name: SendLayer
providers.blurb: SendLayer transactional email API.
providers.note: Find it under Settings → API Keys.

providers.name: SparkPost
providers.blurb: SparkPost transactional email API.
providers.note: The key is shown only once, when you create it. Pick the US or EU region your account is in.

providers.name: SMTP2GO
providers.blurb: SMTP2GO transactional email API.
providers.note: Create it under Sending → API Keys, with Email Send enabled.

providers.name: ZeptoMail
providers.blurb: Zoho ZeptoMail transactional email API.
providers.note: Generated in your Mail Agent once a domain is verified, under Setup Info → API.

providers.name: SocketLabs
providers.blurb: SocketLabs Injection API.
providers.note: The Server ID is the 4- or 5-digit number on your server dashboard. The API key is under Configuration → Key Manager.

providers.name: SendPulse
providers.blurb: SendPulse SMTP API.
providers.note: Both are under Account → API → Client credentials.

providers.name: Bird
providers.blurb: Bird (formerly MessageBird) email API.
providers.note: Create the key under Developers → API keys. The region is the prefix shown with it, such as us1 or eu1.

providers.name: Mailercloud
providers.blurb: Mailercloud transactional Email API.
providers.note: Find it under Account → API Integrations.

providers.name: Sweego
providers.blurb: Sweego email and SMS API.
providers.note: From the Email section of your dashboard. It's shown only once.

providers.name: Emailit
providers.blurb: Emailit transactional email API.
providers.note: Create an API-type credential in your Emailit workspace.

providers.name: Gmail
providers.blurb: Sends through Google's SMTP server using an app password.
providers.note: Needs 2-Step Verification on, and an app password: your normal password won't work.

providers.name: Google Workspace
providers.blurb: Sends through Google's SMTP server using an app password.
providers.note: Needs 2-Step Verification on, and an app password: your normal password won't work.

providers.name: Outlook.com
providers.blurb: Sends through Microsoft's personal-account SMTP server.
providers.note: Use an app password if 2-step verification is on, under Advanced security options → App passwords.

providers.name: Microsoft 365
providers.blurb: Sends through Microsoft 365's business SMTP server.
providers.note: Use an app password if multi-factor authentication is on. Your admin must allow app passwords and SMTP AUTH.

providers.name: Zoho Mail
providers.blurb: Sends through Zoho Mail's SMTP server.
providers.note: Use an app-specific password if two-factor authentication is on, under Security → App Passwords.

providers.name: Yahoo Mail
providers.blurb: Sends through Yahoo Mail's SMTP server.
providers.note: Needs an app password, from Account Security → External connections. Your normal password won't work.

providers.name: iCloud Mail
providers.blurb: Sends through Apple's iCloud Mail SMTP server.
providers.note: Needs an app-specific password, from Sign-In and Security. Your Apple ID password won't work.

providers.name: AOL Mail
providers.blurb: Sends through AOL Mail's SMTP server.
providers.note: Needs an app password, from your AOL Account Security page. Your normal password won't work.

providers.name: Yandex Mail
providers.blurb: Sends through Yandex Mail's SMTP server.
providers.note: Needs an app password, under App passwords. New ones take 2–3 hours to become active.

providers.name: Fastmail
providers.blurb: Sends through Fastmail's SMTP server.
providers.note: Needs an app password, under Settings → Password & Security → App passwords.

providers.name: Titan Email
providers.blurb: Sends through Titan Email's SMTP server.
providers.note: Your Titan Email account password.

providers.name: Purelymail
providers.blurb: Sends through Purelymail's SMTP server.
providers.note: Your Purelymail account password.

providers.name: Migadu
providers.blurb: Sends through Migadu's SMTP server.
providers.note: Your Migadu mailbox password.

providers.name: Namecheap Private Email
providers.blurb: Sends through Namecheap Private Email's SMTP server.
providers.note: Your Private Email mailbox password.

providers.name: Rackspace Email
providers.blurb: Sends through Rackspace Email's SMTP server.
providers.note: Your Rackspace Email mailbox password.

providers.name: Amazon SES
providers.blurb: Sends through Amazon SES's SMTP interface.
providers.note: Use SMTP credentials from the SES console, not your AWS access key. The region, such as us-east-1, must be the one SES is verified in.

providers.name: Amazon WorkMail
providers.blurb: Sends through Amazon WorkMail's SMTP server.
providers.note: The region must match your WorkMail organization's.

providers.name: Cloudflare Email Sending
providers.blurb: Sends through Cloudflare's Email Sending SMTP relay. Your sending domain must already be onboarded for Email Sending on the account that owns the token.
providers.note: Create the token in the Cloudflare dashboard, under Email → Email Routing → Email Sending.

providers.name: Twilio
providers.blurb: Send from a Twilio number, a sender name, or a Messaging Service.
providers.note: A sender starting with MG is sent as a Messaging Service SID.

providers.name: Vonage
providers.blurb: Vonage SMS with automatic Unicode for non-Latin text.
providers.note: Vonage answers 200 for rejected messages, so VuloMail reads the per-message status.

providers.name: Plivo
providers.blurb: Plivo's messaging API.
providers.note: The Auth ID is format-checked before it goes into the request URL.

providers.name: Clickatell
providers.blurb: Clickatell's platform API. Sender is optional.
providers.note: A 202 can still carry a per-message rejection, and VuloMail catches it.

principles.title: Unconfigured means untouched
principles.body: Activating VuloMail changes nothing. WordPress keeps sending as it always has until you set a primary connection.

principles.title: Adapters never throw, never leak
principles.body: A provider failure becomes a clean, failed result with credentials scrubbed out of the error text.

principles.title: Secrets never leave the server
principles.body: Saved keys come back masked. The browser never holds the real value, so it can never send it anywhere.

principles.title: One log row per message
principles.body: Primary, backup, last resort: every attempt is recorded on a single entry, not scattered across many.

principles.title: Privacy by default
principles.body: Message bodies aren't stored unless you opt in. Recipients can be masked. Old entries prune themselves.

faqs.q: Does activating VuloMail change how my site sends email?
faqs.a: No. Nothing changes until you add a connection and set it as primary. Until then WordPress sends exactly as it did before.

faqs.q: Do I need a VuloLabs account or a paid plan?
faqs.a: No. VuloMail is free, has no Pro edition, and contacts no VuloLabs server. You use email and SMS providers you already have.

Everything sent with WordPress's standard wp_mail() function: password resets, new-user emails, comment notifications, WooCommerce order emails, contact form notifications and emails from most plugins. A plugin that talks to an email service directly, without wp_mail(), is not affected.

faqs.q: What do I need to run it?
faqs.a: WordPress 6.4 or newer, PHP 7.4 or newer, an administrator account, and an email account: any SMTP server, one of 22 email APIs such as SendGrid, Postmark or Resend, or a one-click preset such as Gmail, Microsoft 365 or Amazon SES. An SMS provider and WooCommerce are optional.

faqs.q: Does “Sent” mean the email was delivered?
faqs.a: It means your provider accepted it. Delivery to the inbox is reported in your provider's own dashboard, and you can look the message up there using the Provider ID in the log entry.

faqs.q: Will a customer get the same email twice when the backup is used?
faqs.a: Normally no: the backup is only tried when the primary reports a failure. In the rare case where a provider accepts a message but reports an error, the backup would send it again.

faqs.q: What happens when both my primary and backup fail?
faqs.a: With “Fall back to the WordPress default mailer” on (the default), the email is handed to WordPress as a last resort. Switch it off if your host's mailer is unreliable or your provider must be the only sender for your domain.

faqs.q: My emails are sent but land in spam. Why?
faqs.a: Run Tools → Diagnostics and read Sender domain DNS. Add any missing SPF or DMARC record, check DKIM in your provider's dashboard, and use a sender address on your own domain rather than a free mailbox.

faqs.q: Another email plugin is installed. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: Two plugins delivering email compete for the same messages. Diagnostics lists the ones it recognises. To switch: add the same account as a VuloMail connection, set it as primary, send a test, then deactivate the other plugin.
In your WordPress database, encrypted with libsodium. They are never shown again (only dots and the last four characters) and never sent anywhere except to the provider they belong to.

faqs.q: Why does a connection suddenly say “Incomplete”?
faqs.a: Either a required detail is empty, or a saved key can no longer be read. The second happens when the security keys in wp-config.php change, for example after a migration. Edit the connection and enter the key again.

faqs.q: Does VuloMail send my data anywhere?
faqs.a: Only to the providers you connect, and only the messages sent through them. It has no tracking and the delivery log never leaves your site.

faqs.q: Can I use it for marketing text messages?
faqs.a: VuloMail sends what your site asks it to. You are responsible for having your recipients' consent and for the rules on text messages in your country.

faqs.q: Why was my text message rejected for an invalid number?
faqs.a: Numbers should be in international format, like +14155550123. If your customers enter numbers without a country code, set a Default country code under Settings → SMS.

faqs.q: How long can a text message be?
faqs.a: Up to 1,530 characters. A text over 160 plain characters is billed as two or more messages, and emoji or non-Latin scripts lower that to 70. Every alert template shows its placeholders so you can keep messages short.

faqs.q: What happens to my data if I uninstall?
faqs.a: Deactivating never deletes anything. When you delete the plugin, your data is kept by default. Choose Settings → Data → Delete everything first if you want the table, settings and connections removed.
